text: Solomon didn't ask for wisdom in general. He asked for "an understanding heart": in Hebrew, a hearing heart.
explanation:
When God said, "Ask! What shall I give you?", young Solomon asked for a lev shomea, a hearing heart, to judge God's people. He'd learned from his father where wisdom lives: "In the hidden part You will make me to know wisdom"; the ESV says, "in the secret heart." And Solomon went on to surpass every king of his time in wisdom and wealth.

People chase lottery numbers thinking money will buy security, happiness or health. What they really want is what wisdom gives: long life, riches, honour, pleasant paths and peace. Go straight to the source. Ask God for a heart that hears Him.

text: "The heart is desperately wicked" describes the old heart. God promised, "I will give you a new heart."
explanation:
Many believers have been taught never to trust their hearts. After his sin with Bathsheba, David prayed, "Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a steadfast spirit within me." He knew the problem wasn't a lack of discipline; it was his heart. Through Ezekiel, God promised a covenant that would answer that prayer: "I will take the heart of stone out of your flesh and give you a heart of flesh."

If you're born again, you have that new heart. Old habits may linger in the flesh, like a monastery bell you keep hearing in your head long after it's stopped ringing. But the old nature is gone, and God has put His wisdom in your new heart. You can learn to listen to it.

text: "Jesus perceived in His spirit that they reasoned within themselves." Perceiving and reasoning are different things.
explanation:
When Jesus forgave the paralysed man, the scribes began reasoning, dialogizomai, the root of our word logic: "Who can forgive sins but God alone?" Jesus perceived it, knowing clearly within. Paul prays that "the eyes of your understanding" would be enlightened; the word is dianoia, the part of you that sees.

The Bible never uses dialogizomai of Jesus. Reasoning has its place, but let it serve you, not lead you. Have you ever met someone saying all the right words and felt deep down that something wasn't right? Listen to that, even when you can't explain it. You often see things long before you can reason them out.

text: "I will put My laws in their mind and write them on their hearts." God's guidance in the new covenant comes from within.
explanation:
The "mind" in Hebrews 8 is dianoia again: the seeing part of you. Under the old covenant, God's laws were carved on stone outside. Under the new, He writes on your heart. "None of them shall teach his neighbour… saying, 'Know the Lord,' for all shall know Me." John adds, "You have an anointing from the Holy One, and you know all things."

That's why so many people hear grace preached and say, "I always knew it was like this." The preacher confirms what God has already written inside. Be wary of anyone who claims to direct your life when nothing in your spirit agrees. Outside words should confirm, not dictate.

text: In a heated conversation, that inner "stop now" isn't a suggestion to add three more sentences.
explanation:
Most of us know the moment. The discussion with your spouse is getting heated, and something inside says, "Stop here." We hear "stop" as "after one more point," and that's the sentence that does the damage. The same inner voice says "enough" at episode three of the series, or hour four at the mall, or when the talk turns to gossip.

The Spirit's leading isn't there to spoil your fun. It frees you from stress you don't even know you're carrying. In 2019, Joseph Prince kept sensing he shouldn't book the church's Israel trip for the following year, and cancelled it. Then the pandemic came. Following that inner witness is what walking in rest looks like.

text: In Leviticus 23, before any of Israel's seven feasts, God speaks of the Sabbath. Rest comes before celebration.
explanation:
Many teach on Israel's seven feasts but skip the verses that come first: "Six days shall work be done, but the seventh day is a Sabbath of solemn rest." Likewise in Exodus 35, before listing the skilled, willing workers who built the tabernacle, God first commands the Sabbath.

You can't celebrate properly until you know how to rest, and you can't work effectively for God until you've first received from Him. Don't praise God as a technique to twist His arm. Rest in what He's done, then praise Him for it, and you'll find He keeps blessing you. You can never out-give Him.

text: "You are an epistle of Christ… written not with ink but by the Spirit… on tablets of flesh, that is, of the heart."
explanation:
Most people around you will never read the Bible. But they read you. As God's Word is preached by the Spirit, it's being written on your heart, and you become a living letter: a colleague notices your kindness, a neighbour senses your peace, someone hears your testimony of freedom from addiction.

The world doesn't need more arguments; people who are lost can usually out-argue you. They need to see something real: joy in your eyes, love they can feel, a radiance that comes from Christ in you. When people read the letter of your life, let it lead them to the Author.
